test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 16 Feb 2021 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: What are the criteria to be considered to get Maharatna status?

options.text: Having positive net profit to net worth ratio

solution:
The correct answer is __**Having significant global presence/international operations**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• To be eligible for the **Maharatna status**, a company must have a **significant global presence/international operations**.
 
• Other criteria include having a **Miniratna Category-1 status**, a **positive net profit to net worth ratio**, and **inter-sectoral performance**.
 
• The status is granted to Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs) in India, allowing them greater autonomy in decision-making.
 
• Maharatna status is aimed at enabling CPSEs to expand their operations and emerge as global giants.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Maharatna status** was introduced by the Government of India in December 2009 to empower mega CPSEs to expand their operations and emerge as global giants.
 
• Currently, there are several CPSEs that have been granted Maharatna status, including ONGC, Indian Oil Corporation, and NTPC.
 
• With this status, these enterprises have enhanced powers to invest in joint ventures and subsidiaries and to undertake mergers and acquisitions.
 
• Companies with Maharatna status can invest up to 15% of their net worth in a single project without seeking government approval, subject to a cap of ₹5,000 crores.
